Live 3D globe · Taaza NASA FIRMS snapshot · sabse taaza guzar 25 Oct 2026, 3:19 PM IST

India in 3D — is it burning right now?

This globe shows only the last 24 hours — every thermal hotspot NASA’s VIIRS and MODIS satellites detected across India in the 24 hours before the freshest pass (25 Oct 2026, 3:19 PM IST), glowing by strength and fading as it ages: a dot older than 24 hours leaves this view entirely, because most such dots were short crop-stubble burns that are long out. Nothing from history is plotted here: past disasters appear only when you search their date below, never mixed into the live view. Drag to spin it, scroll or pinch to zoom into any corner of the country — tap any dot and it states the exact date and time (IST) it was seen. The view re-scans every 5 minutes, amber diamonds mark the areas where new fires look most likely, and the checker below the globe answers for any place in India against the full snapshot: how many hotspots are near it, how strong, where the nearest one is, and what the fire risk looks like there. Prefer a flat map? Switch to the 2D view, same live window.

Dots ka matlab — simple guide
Bada chamakta dot = tez aag (15 MW+). DHYAAN DO — tap karo, dhuaan-cloud khulega.
Chhota halka dot = kamzor nishan — aam taur par parali / khet ki jalai. IGNORE kar sakte ho.
Peela diamond = khatre wala ilaaka (risk zone) — yahan nayi aag lagne ke chances zyada.
Laal dhadakta spot = tumhari chuni hui jagah / khula hua record.

The full record

India’s major fire disasters, 1979–2026

One hundred and ten disasters, each one verified against published reports — government records, court and inquiry coverage, BBC and national newspapers — before it entered this archive: the date, the place, the toll. Open any card to stand at the spot on the globe and see the record in full.

Lives lost, by decade

Recorded deaths across the archive’s 110 disasters. The 1990s peak is driven by two mass gatherings — Dabwali (442) and Baripada (176).

How this works

Real data, honestly labelled

Live fire picture

Hotspots come from NASA FIRMS (VIIRS (Suomi-NPP + NOAA-20) + MODIS, near-real-time feed) for the India region. Points falling outside India’s landmass are filtered out before plotting; the snapshot on this page covers 24–25 October 2026 and every detection carries its real date and time. The live globe and 2D map plot only the last 24 hours before the freshest pass — older detections stay in the snapshot for the area checker and date search, but are never presented as burning now, because a satellite passes over India only a few times a day and most small detections are short crop-stubble burns. Fire radiative power (FRP, in megawatts) is the satellite’s measure of how strongly a fire is burning.

The disaster archive

Each of the 110 records was checked against its published source — government records (Parliament answers, NGT, CPCB, NHRC), Wikipedia incident reports, BBC and national newspaper coverage — which is linked on every record. Photos are genuine news photographs of the event or its site, verified one by one before inclusion; where a verified copy could not be secured, the record links straight to the coverage instead of showing a substitute. Every disaster that has passed verification so far is man-made. No natural (wildfire) disaster currently meets the verification bar, because reported tolls for events like the 2016 Uttarakhand forest fires conflict across sources — wildfires themselves are tracked in the live snapshot above.

Meet Agni, the assistant

Tap the flame button and ask in your own words — type or speak. Try “What happened on 13 June 1997?”, “Sabse badi aag kab lagi thi?”, “Show me hospital fires”, or “Is anything burning today?”. Agni searches this same archive and the live snapshot, answers aloud if you want, and opens the place for you.

In a real fire emergency, call 101 (Fire) or 112 (all emergencies).
This website is an information and awareness archive — it does not dispatch help.

India Fire Explorer

Live satellite fire watch for India, and a verified archive of the country’s major fire disasters, 1979–2026. Built so that these days are remembered with facts — and so the next one is caught earlier.

Data sources

  • NASA FIRMS — VIIRS (Suomi-NPP + NOAA-20) + MODIS active fire data
  • Incident records — Wikipedia & national news reports (linked on each record)
  • Photographs — credited news archives, verified per event
